stemMd: At the same depth in the same stationary liquid, how does pressure compare in a wide vessel and a narrow vessel open to the atmosphere?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It is proportional only to total liquid volume.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It is always larger in the narrower vessel.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It is zero in the narrow vessel.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It is always larger in the wider vessel.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It is the same in both.

explanationMd: Hydrostatic pressure is atmospheric pressure plus ρgh. Both vessels have the same surface pressure, liquid density and depth, so the pressures are equal. Vessel shape affects total force on surfaces but not pressure at a specified depth.

distractorRationale.d: Hydrostatic pressure depends on depth and density, not vessel width.
distractorRationale.b: Narrowness alone does not increase hydrostatic pressure.
distractorRationale.a: Equal depth can give equal pressure despite different volumes.
